title: "Recipe: Adopt a release from the staged ladder (alpha → rc → GA)"
toc-title: Recipe
---

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tool | kailash (releases / nixos-rebuild) |
| Section | Administrator |
| Level | medium |
| Time | ~30 min review + rebuild |
| Layer/Category | admin (whole-system) |
| Tags | `admin`, `release`, `versioning`, `YYYY.NN`, `rollback` |


## Problem

Kailash releases move along a staged ladder — `2026.01-alpha.1` →
`2026.01-rc.1` → bare `2026.01` (GA) → dotted re-cuts. The operator
decides which rung the host should pin. A lab VM tolerates an alpha.
A published-results machine (attestations, assessments, the book's
verification legs) should ride rc or GA. The bare name carries a
meaning ("general availability, full review posture"). So the WRONG
rung, or a staged cut misread as GA, silently weakens what the
operator can state about the system.

## Solution

Read the ladder honestly (`git tag -v` shows the stage). Adopt the
tag that matches the posture. Keep the escape hatch (generation
rollback) one reboot away:

```bash
# 1. See the ladder as tags, with signatures verified
git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os | tail
git tag -v 2026.01-rc.1        # stage + increment visible in the verified tag
git tag -v 2026.01             # bare name = GA (full artefact matrix posture)

# 2. Pick the rung per posture:
#      lab/experiment VM .......... latest -alpha.N  (iterate freely,
#                                    documented gaps are the deal)
#      published-work machine ..... latest -rc.N     (the GA-readiness gate:
#                                    the standing release checklist filled in
#                                    FULL, artefact matrix + SHA256SUMS
#                                    complete at the tag)
#      anything you must be able to state plainly . bare YYYY.NN (GA)

# 3. Adopt it — pin the flake at the tag, then rebuild
#    (host configuration or flake input, per your setup):
#      inputs.kailash-os.url = "github:kailash-os/kailash-os/2026.01-rc.1";
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#<host>

# 4. Prove what you got (the truthfulness chain from
#    [Boot a verified release image](../getting-started/first-image.html)):
nix flake metadata github:kailash-os/kailash-os/2026.01-rc.1 | head -5
nix build github:kailash-os/kailash-os/2026.01-rc.1 \
    #kailash-images-qemu-full --no-link --print-out-paths
kailash manifest validate

# 5. Version sanity: the lock tells you which train you are on
nix flake metadata github:kailash-os/kailash-os/2026.01-rc.1 \
    | grep -A1 '"rev"'   # the locked packages rev == what the release notes state
```

Expected output shape (abridged):

```
$ git tag -v 2026.01-rc.1
object ... type commit
tag 2026.01-rc.1
Tagger: Kailash Release <releases@kailash.os>
<gpg: Good signature from ...>
<release-notes text>
# (a staged cut says so in its own verified tag text — an alpha/rc
#  NEVER reads as GA)
```

What success looks like:

- `git tag -v` verifies a good signature on every considered rung
- the staged cuts carry `-alpha.N` / `-rc.N` suffixes — the bare
  `2026.NN` does NOT appear until GA
- the adopted tag's release notes carry the checklist evidence the
  rung promises
- rc: full checklist; alpha: the reduced §7.9 artefact set with
  stated gaps
- `kailash manifest validate` is green on the rebuilt system
- the previous generation is still in the boot menu

## Discussion

- **The three stages differ by commitment, not by form.** An
  `-alpha.N` cut iterates freely — the reduced artefact set may ship
  with explicitly-documented gaps and punctual attestations. `-rc.N`
  is the GA-readiness gate: the standing release checklist filled in
  full. The train's backlog disposition is recorded (ride with
  evidence or explicit re-scope). The artefact matrix is complete at
  the tag, with SHA256SUMS covering every artefact. GA is the bare
  tag after an rc. A material change in between makes `rc.N+1`
  first. A rushed GA is what the ladder exists to prevent.
- **Names are load-bearing.** Bare `YYYY.NN` is RESERVED for GA.
  A material re-cut of a shipped GA posts `YYYY.NN.1` only when a
  shipped artefact actually changes. Changelog-notes-only re-cuts
  keep the tag. NN is the release index within the year's train —
  not the calendar month (`2026.02` may GA in January 2027). No
  gaps, no renames: a slipping RC renumbers nothing.
- **Adoption is one of the two ways to move forward in the update
  model.** The operator rebuilds against a newer lock at the
  operator's own cadence, or adopts a released lock bump as-is.
  This recipe is the second way. Its lock-review mechanics are the
  first — see
  [Ride a release without breaking pinned tooling](updates.html).
- **Generation rollback is the safety net, not a version pin:** an
  adoption that disappoints is restarted, not untangled. Boot the
  previous generation, then re-decide the rung. Backups of anything
  outside the store (lab data mounted the normal way) sit in the
  operator's own lane. The system itself is a generation.
- **Name the rung in every result report:** findings, scan reports
  and attestations name the tag. A published claim with an
  unspecified ladder rung is not reproducible. The CLI's per-tool
  provenance report (manifest-informed `kailash doctor`) is the
  roadmap verb. The landed slice: list/search/info/profile
  list/manifest validate. The tag plus the lock delta are the
  provenance records that exist today. The adopted tag is the
  version every page in this book verifies against.
